clips.text_zh: 又係啲叫人死揸嘅post。一星期後你就會知點解你死揸XRP、BTC、DOGE⋯⋯OK fine，我自己都係輸緊，當係交學費囉。考牌都未搞掂，搞prop firm真係好蠢🧐
clips.text_en_b1: In one week you will know why you held XRP, BTC, and DOGE through the toughest five years any investor has ever faced. The poster says the payoff is coming soon. Anyone holding these three knows the pain has been real. It came up on /biz/ today.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ anon preaching patience to XRP/BTC/DOGE holders

signal.rationale: Poster argues the toughest stretch is over and a payoff is imminent

clips.text_en_b2: In a week, you’ll finally understand why you held XRP, BTC, and DOGE through what the poster calls the most brutal five years any investor has had to endure. He insists that the payoff is just around the corner, although the people still holding these coins know the pain has been painfully real. It is yet another classic “hold through the pain” post, and it appeared on /biz/ today.
clips.text_en_c1: Within a week, you will come to understand precisely why holding XRP, BTC, and DOGE through what can only be described as the most punishing five-year stretch in modern investing will have vindicated those who refused to capitulate. The original poster insists that the long-awaited payoff is imminent, a claim that has predictably drawn scepticism from the board. Yet anyone who has actually ridden out the drawdowns knows the suffering has been visceral rather than rhetorical. The thread, which surfaced on /biz/ today, blends genuine conviction with the kind of cope that markets breed when conviction runs dry and tuition fees pile up.
clips.text_en_c2: In roughly a week's time, the speculative thesis will have been thoroughly vindicated — or so the original poster contends — because anyone who steadfastly held XRP, BTC, and DOGE across what can only be described as the most punishing five-year stretch any retail investor has endured is now poised, allegedly, to reap the long-deferred rewards. The argument, circulated on /biz/, is that the present pain, however excruciating, is merely the antecedent to an imminent breakout, and that those three tokens in particular represent a kind of generational conviction trade. The author himself, characteristically, concedes that he remains underwater and frames the position as tuition paid rather than capital preserved; his licence, he notes dryly, remains uncertified, and his prop-firm ambitions were, in retrospect, probably rather foolish.

clips.text_zh: 聯儲局唔會加息。Warsh扮嘢話認真對付通脹，Bessent就買yen仲暗示會掟一萬億出嚟⋯⋯Trump又鬧Powell太遲cut rate。OK，DXY應該會跌，gold又可以睇下🙏
clips.text_en_b1: The Federal Reserve is NOT going to hike. Warsh talks about an inflation taskforce but does nothing. Bessent buys yen and hints he might dump a trillion into buybacks. Trump criticises Powell for being too late to cut rates. The economy is good, so rates should fall.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ breakdown of Warsh, Bessent and Trump pressuring Powell

signal.rationale: Anons see coordinated pressure for a weaker dollar and rate cuts

clips.text_en_b2: The Federal Reserve is not going to hike interest rates. Warsh can talk as much as he likes about taking inflation seriously, but the poster thinks his so-called taskforce will achieve precisely nothing. Meanwhile, Bessent is buying yen and apparently hinting that he might dump a trillion into buybacks. Trump, for his part, is still criticising Powell for cutting rates too slowly.
clips.text_en_c1: The Federal Reserve is categorically not going to raise rates, regardless of how hawkish certain appointees attempt to posture. Warsh grandstands about forming an inflation-fighting taskforce whilst presiding over precisely zero concrete action, and Bessent has been quietly accumulating yen while obliquely hinting that a trillion-dollar liquidity injection could materialise if circumstances demand it. Meanwhile Trump continues to lambaste Powell for moving too cautiously on cuts, a delay he frames as politically motivated. With the underlying economy holding up reasonably well, the logical conclusion is that the dollar index should soften and gold merits another careful look from anyone positioning for the next rotation.
clips.text_en_c2: The Federal Reserve, contrary to the prevailing hawkish consensus articulated across much of the financial press, is most emphatically not going to hike — at least not according to a thread that surfaced on /biz/ today. The argument hinges on a constellation of seemingly contradictory signals: Warsh postures about establishing a dedicated inflation task force yet undertakes nothing of substance; Bessent, meanwhile, accumulates yen positions while floating the prospect of deploying upwards of a trillion in buyback liquidity. Layered onto this is Trump's characteristic excoriation of Powell for moving too slowly on rate cuts, an intervention that, given the underlying economic resilience of the United States, only reinforces the dovish inference. The conclusion — DXY softens, gold merits another look.

clips.text_zh: 個post話如果AI真係咁得，班政府一早傾緊UBI啦，但而家乜都冇做，所以AI最多都係食1%嘅工。WTF，我surveying嘅位都驚畀人搶😩 靠AI續命
clips.text_en_b1: If AI could really do what people say, every government would be urgently discussing UBI right now, but they are not. Not one government is doing anything about supposed job losses. This tells the poster that AI will take less than 1% of jobs. He feels sorry for the plebs who fell for the marketing.
clips.source_hint: /g/ anon argues AI job loss hype is just marketing
clips.text_en_b2: If AI could genuinely replace workers on the scale its promoters keep suggesting, governments would already be scrambling to introduce universal basic income. The fact that none of them are doing anything meaningful about mass job losses supposedly proves that AI will eliminate less than one percent of employment. That is the poster’s argument, although the idea sounds far more convincing to him than it does to everyone else.
clips.text_en_c1: Were artificial intelligence genuinely capable of displacing workers on the scale that breathless commentators insist upon, one would reasonably expect every government in the developed world to be scrambling to legislate universal basic income as a matter of existential urgency. The conspicuous absence of such proposals tells the original poster everything he needs to know, which is that AI will ultimately consume well under one percent of employment, contrary to the panic being marketed to credulous audiences. His own surveying position is by no means insulated from the anxiety, though he concedes the doomer narrative has been weaponised against people who cannot afford to ignore it.
clips.text_en_c2: The poster's argument is, on its face, disarmingly simple: had artificial intelligence genuinely possessed the labour-substituting capabilities so breathlessly advertised by its evangelists, every sitting government on earth would, by now, have convened emergency consultations on universal basic income — and conspicuously, none have. The absence of any such policy deliberation is, in his estimation, dispositive evidence that the displacement narrative has been substantially overstated, and that genuine white-collar attrition will almost certainly fall well short of one percent of total employment. He reserves particular scorn for the credulous masses who, seduced by vendor marketing, have apparently internalised catastrophist projections wholesale. He himself, an surveyor by trade, concedes a residual disquiet about his own position, though his professional survival, for the moment, remains contingent upon AI-augmented workflows.

clips.text_zh: CHINA要DROP美元掛鈎，今晚轉咗YUAN去peg油價。寫post嗰個人話你哋太蠢唔知呢樣嘢會改變晒成個game⋯⋯OK wtf，我CFD倉會唔會又爆一鑊🧐
clips.text_en_b1: CHINA IS DROPPING THE DOLLAR PEG TONIGHT. CHINA NOW PEGS THE YUAN TO THE PRICE OF CRUDE OIL AND YOU ARE TOO DUMB TO KNOW THAT THIS CHANGES EVERYTHING. The poster claims the yuan is now tied to oil instead of the US dollar. This came up on /pol/ today.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ doom post about China pegging yuan to crude oil

signal.rationale: Viral conspiracist post, no factual basis, no setup

clips.text_en_b2: According to the post, China is dropping the dollar peg tonight and switching the yuan to a crude-oil-based system instead. The author keeps shouting that the rest of us are too stupid to realise this will change the entire game, as though the claim were already an established fact rather than an unsupported prediction. The basic claim is that the yuan is now tied to oil prices, not the US dollar.
clips.text_en_c1: CHINA IS SEVERING THE DOLLAR PEG AS OF TONIGHT. The yuan is to be reanchored directly to the price of crude oil, a tectonic monetary recalibration that, according to the original poster, the overwhelming majority of retail spectators are far too dim to appreciate before it fundamentally reshapes every market they participate in. The claim, posted to /pol/ earlier today, has predictably attracted equal measures of derision and alarm from respondents who recognise the magnitude of such a revaluation. If even a fraction of the rumour proves accurate, the implications for leveraged positions and existing CFD exposures could be catastrophically asymmetric.
clips.text_en_c2: CHINA IS ABANDONING THE DOLLAR PEG — TONIGHT. The yuan, according to an impassioned and rather triumphalist dispatch on /pol/, is henceforth to be anchored not to the greenback but, in a development that the author insists will fundamentally recalibrate the entire geopolitical settlement, to the spot price of crude oil itself. The conceit is, to put it charitably, ambitious: a re-pegged renminbi would ostensibly sever the petrodollar arrangement that has underwritten American monetary hegemony since Bretton Woods, and thereby confer upon Beijing a leverage it has long been presumed to covet. Investors holding yuan-denominated CFDs, the poster included, are left to contemplate whether their positions are about to be summarily liquidated in the crossfire. His tone suggests they probably are.

clips.text_zh: lol，個trailer同官網完全冇列出developer，咁Nintendo究竟外判咗畀邊個？⋯⋯我都係繼續睇S15算啦，肥仔信今日又叫我去打rank🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Does NO ONE find it suspicious that the developer is not listed anywhere in the trailer, website, or promotional materials? Who did Nintendo outsource this to? Players are asking why the studio name is missing from every official channel. It came up on /v/ today.
clips.source_hint: /v/ thread about mystery Nintendo outsourced project
clips.text_en_b2: Does nobody find it slightly suspicious that the developer is missing from the trailer, the official website, and every other piece of promotional material? Players are naturally asking who Nintendo outsourced the project to, especially when the studio name has vanished from every official channel. The absence may be deliberate, but it could also indicate that the production arrangement was changed late in development. Either way, the trailer gives us almost nothing to work with, so everyone is left speculating.
clips.text_en_c1: Is nobody remotely bothered by the conspicuous absence of any developer credit across the trailer, the official website, or any of the promotional materials that Nintendo has disseminated for this title? The studio responsible for the project has been entirely redacted from every channel through which such information would ordinarily be disclosed, a silence that has prompted players to speculate openly about which third-party outfit the publisher has quietly engaged. The thread on /v/ has coalesced around the suspicion that the omission is deliberate, and the prevailing mood veers between distrust and indifference as the userbase awaits further clarification.
clips.text_en_c2: It is, the poster observes with no particular malice, faintly curious that Nintendo has chosen to omit the development studio from every conceivable promotional surface — neither the cinematic trailer, nor the official website, nor any of the accompanying press materials so much as hazard a credit. The conspicuous anonymity has, predictably, given rise to a vigorous /v/ thread speculating as to which external partner has been entrusted with what is, by all appearances, a tentpole release. Speculation has ranged from established Western studios to anonymous Korean shops, though Nintendo itself has, in keeping with its institutional temperament, declined to dignify any of it with a clarification. The poster, displaying the quiet pragmatism endemic to the board, has elected to invest his evening in the ongoing Season 15 grind instead.

clips.text_zh: 廢柴⋯⋯我OHP就嚟到1pl8但bench仲未到2pl8，squat 3pl8都未得，deadlift 4pl8更加唔使講。肥仔信話我一個月內應該rep到1pl8 OHP⋯⋯lol，等我練多陣先啦🙏
clips.text_en_b1: The poster is closer to a 1 plate OHP than he is to a 2 plate bench, a 3 plate squat, or a 4 plate deadlift. He thinks he will hit a 1 plate OHP for reps in a month or two. His other lifts are all still behind. It came up on /fit/ today.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ progress post about OHP getting close to 1 plate

signal.rationale: Personal lifting log, no trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: I’m getting pretty close to pressing a one-plate overhead barbell, yet my bench is still nowhere near two plates, my squat has not reached three, and a four-plate deadlift is completely out of the question. Basically, I’m specialising in the one lift that makes me look least impressive, while my supposedly essential numbers continue to drag behind.
clips.text_en_c1: The poster finds himself in the unenviable position of being tantalisingly close to a one-plate overhead press whilst his compound lifts have lagged considerably behind, with his bench press still shy of two plates, his squat stubbornly refusing to breach the three-plate threshold, and his deadlift nowhere near four. He estimates, with a degree of cautious optimism encouraged by his coach, that a clean single-plate OHP for reps ought to materialise within the next month or so. The remaining milestones, however, remain aspirational rather than imminent, and he has elected to consolidate his pressing progress before chasing the heavier squats further down the line.
clips.text_en_c2: The poster's lifting trajectory is, by his own rueful admission, an exercise in physiological asymmetry — the overhead press, that most stubbornly recalcitrant of compound movements, is tantalisingly close to a one-plate milestone, whereas the bench press languishes somewhere south of two plates, the squat has yet to breach three, and the deadlift, that most forgiving of barbell lifts, remains a distant four-plate aspiration. A friend, charitably described as the resident gym-bro oracle, has opined that a clean single-plate rep on the OHP ought to fall within the next month or two, provided the requisite accessories are diligently programmed. The poster, displaying a commendable instinct for self-preservation, intends to honour the process and defer any premature celebration until the bar has actually cleared his frontal plane.

clips.text_zh: 週刊少年Magazine第41期，2026年。Yowayowa嘅彩色頁有新連載Onryou Biyori。OK，gundam 00都追完一排，等我有時間再睇🙏
clips.text_en_b1: WSM (Weekly Shonen Magazine), issue no. 41, 2026. The colour pages are for Yowayowa, and a new manga called Onryou Biyori is launching. This came up on /a/ today for readers tracking new serialisations.
clips.source_hint: /a/ scanlation news about WSM issue 41 new serialisation

signal.rationale: Manga industry news, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: Weekly Shonen Magazine issue 41, released in 2026, includes colour pages for Yowayowa and is also launching a new manga series titled Onryou Biyori. That sounds like useful information for anyone trying to keep track of new serialisations, especially since the magazine’s schedule is packed enough for smaller titles to disappear without warning. Still, I have finally finished watching Gundam 00 after sticking with it for ages, so I am not exactly desperate to start another long-running series.
clips.text_en_c1: The forty-first issue of Weekly Shonen Magazine for 2026 has landed, and the colour pages have been allocated to Yowayowa alongside the launch announcement for an intriguing new serialisation bearing the title Onryou Biyori, whose premise has already generated a modest amount of speculation among regular readers. With Gundam 00 having finally concluded its latest run and the backlog of unread volumes continuing to accumulate, the poster confesses that he will need to carve out a genuinely unhurried afternoon before he can do justice to the new chapter in question, a luxury his current schedule conspicuously fails to provide.
clips.text_en_c2: Weekly Shonen Magazine, issue forty-one of the 2026 editorial calendar, has landed with its customary mid-autumn payload — chief among the featured attractions being a lavishly produced colour spread courtesy of Yowayowa, whose stylistic sensibilities continue to command an unusually devoted following among the readership. Bolting onto the schedule, as these things so often do at the eleventh hour, is a brand-new serialisation entitled Onryou Biyori, the premise of which appears, judging by the table of contents, to involve malevolent spirits operating in a contemporary high-school register. The post itself, surfacing on /a/ among the usual coterie of serialisation trackers, notes in passing that Gundam 00 has likewise been concluded, thereby freeing up the poster's already constrained leisure hours for what he charitably describes as eventual reading.
